1139: \subsection{Production and decay of quark-lepton composite bosons $\Pi^{5/3,-1/3,2/3}_a$}
1140: 
1141: As already specified in Sec.~\ref{contact}, 
1142: the quark-lepton composite bosons $\Pi$ can be 
1143: \begin{eqnarray}
1144: &&\Pi^{5/3}_a ~(\bar eu,\bar \mu c, \bar\tau \replaced[id=SH]{t}{b}),\nonumber\\
1145: &&\Pi^{-1/3}_a ~(\bar \nu^e d,\bar \nu^\mu s, \bar \nu^\mu \replaced[id=SH]{b}{t}),\nonumber\\
1146: &&\Pi^{2/3}_{u_a} ~(\bar \nu^e u,\bar \nu^\mu c, \bar \nu^\tau \replaced[id=SH]{t}{b}),\nonumber\\ 
1147: &&\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a} ~(\bar ed,\bar \mu s, \bar \tau b),
1148: \label{comSpecBql}
1149: \end{eqnarray}
1150: for the charge sector $Q=+5/3,-1/3,2/3$ 
1151: respectively, and the corresponding composite bosons 
1152: of the higher generation of families in the SM.
1153: 
1154: The kinematics of the processes is derived in the center of mass frame of $pp$ collisions and virtual processes 
1155: of $\Pi$ are not considered. If the energy $\sqrt{s}$ in the parton centre of mass frame is larger than composite boson masses, the following resonant process can occur:
1156: \begin{eqnarray}
1157: p~e &\rightarrow&  ~\Pi_a
1158: \label{ppfFBql}
1159: \end{eqnarray}
1160: where the composite bosons $\Pi_a$ (\ref{comSpecB}) formed by Standard Model fermions 
1161: of the higher generation of families. The kinematics of final states is simple in the centre of mass frame of $ep$ collisions.
1162: 
1163: If we neglect the quark-family mixing, the previous process can manifest at parton level as:
1164: \begin{eqnarray}
1165: u~\bar e &\rightarrow& \Pi^{5/3}_a,\label{udBql}\\
1166: d~\bar\nu^e &\rightarrow& \Pi^{-1/3}_a,\label{udbarBql}\\
1167: u~\bar\nu^e &\rightarrow&  \Pi^{2/3}_a, \label{uuBql}\\
1168: d~\bar{e} &\rightarrow& \Pi^{2/3}_a.\label{ddBql}
1169: 
1170: 
1171: \end{eqnarray}
1172: We find that the quark-lepton composite bosons $\Pi^{5/3}_a$ and $\Pi^{2/3}_a$ can be produced by $ep$ collisions.
1173: 
1174: The composite boson $\Pi_a$ can decay through the different channels: 
1175: SM quark $q$ and lepton $\ell$, via the contact 
1176: interactions in Eqs.~(\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBuql}). 
1177: Then the composite fermion $\Pi$ decays as:
1178: \begin{eqnarray}
1179: \Pi_a~&\rightarrow& ~ \ell ~q ,\label{FqqBql} 
1180: \end{eqnarray}
1181: the branching ratio of this decay is the approximately same as 
1182: the decay of the $\Pi^{0,\pm}(\bar q q)$, which has been calculated. 
1183: The full decay chain is:
1184: \begin{eqnarray}
1185: e~p &\rightarrow& \Pi_a  \rightarrow ~ \ell q.
1186: \end{eqnarray}
1187: 
1188: It appears clear, considering all the possible flavours of $\Pi_a$ (\ref{comSpecBql}), that a large range 
1189: of final states is possible. 
1190: The cross section of the process $ep \rightarrow \Pi_a $, the decay branching ratios of $\Pi_a$, and the final states and their topologies are discussed below. Composite bosons and quark-lepton composite bosons have same cross sections and decay rates, by exchanging (\ref{quarklepton}).
1191: 
1192: Note that Quark-lepton composite bosons do not possess contact interactions with SM gauge bosons like (\ref{cpg}-\ref{cpgg}).

1204: leptoquark composite bosons ($[T^a,T^b]=if^{abc}T^c$ and $\tr (T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2$),

1212: \end{eqnarray}
1213: as shown in Francesco slide \ref{leptoq_1}. This is the gluon-gluon collision producing two leptoquark bosons, kinematically, CM energy of two gluons should be larger than $2M_{\Pi}$.

1215: Analogously, the gluon and composite fermion interacting Lagrangian is from

1217: \begin{eqnarray}
1218:  + ig_3T^a A^a_\mu \bar F^Q_R \gamma^\mu F^Q_R + ig_3T^a A^a_\mu \bar F^Q_L \gamma^\mu F^Q_L,\label{ggpp}

1223: \end{eqnarray}

## Objective

## Important Details

- Directory inventory: `TASK.md`, `SM.fr`, `frgen`, `tools/fr_lint.py`, `tools/frgen/{__init__.py,render.py,frmodel.py,templates/model.fr.j2}`, `paper/2311.18472_source.tex`.
- SCHEMA RULES (TASK.md): all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups []`; standard indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need NO declaration; any other index needs `index_decls` (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); unique `class_index` per particle; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields, true for real/Majorana; new coupling/mixing parameters External unless clearly derived; `lagrangian_terms` verbatim Mathematica strings (FeynRules idioms); COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — all multiplets/mass eigenstates/generations as separate ParticleClass entries **or class_members** (class_members counts).
- frmodel.py schema facts: pydantic `FeynRulesModel, GaugeGroup, IndexDecl, MassSpec, Parameter, ParticleClass`; `NumberStr = str`; helper `unbalanced(text)` validates bracket balance skipping Mathematica strings and nested `(* *)` comments; structure M$Parameters/M$ClassesDescription/M$GaugeGroups/M$Information/IndexRange, carry Lagrangian/mixing/NLO as verbatim strings. Full field names still unseen (read truncated at ~line 45 both times).

  - `fieldless_term` (stage mg5): every non-total term's RHS must contain ≥1 declared new class name or bar. ⇒ do NOT emit SM-only terms (SM Yukawas etc.); SM.fr supplies them. Only emit terms containing ≥1 new field (kinetic+mass terms for every new particle qualify).
  - Name blocklists (rule 10): avoid `FR_SYMBOLS` (HC, CC, FS, DC, del, Eps, Ga, ProjP, ProjM, T, Sig, PauliSigma, IndexDelta, ME, Index, Indices, Mass, Width, Value, Unphysical, Abelian) and `PROTECTED` (N, C, D, E, I, K, O, Pi, Gamma, Beta, Zeta, Sqrt, Exp, Log, Sin, Cos, Tan, Re, Im, Conjugate, Sum, Block, Module, Table, If, Which).
  - Rule 14 single root: `LTotal` must reference every other term name; term names must start with `L` (`^(L\w+)\s*:?=`).
  - `undeclared_symbol` warn for capitalized symbols used with `.` or `[` not declared — minimize bare SM-field usage; residual warnings acceptable if judged harmless.
- Physics inventory (verified):
  - Π^{0,±} complex scalars; definitions Π^+ = (g*/F_Π)²(d̄^a_R u_La), Π^- = (g*/F_Π)²(ū^a_R d_La), Π^0_u = (g*/F_Π)²(ū^a_R u_La), Π^0_d = (g*/F_Π)²(d̄^a_R d_La); normalized field has dimension [energy]; color index summed.
  - Quantum numbers (Table `qnuP0`): Π^+ Q=+1,t3=+1/2,Y=+1/2; Π^- Q=-1,t3=-1/2,Y=-1/2; Π^0_u Q=0,t3=+1/2,Y=-1/2; Π^0_d Q=0,t3=-1/2,Y=+1/2.

  - Widths: Γ(Π→qq′) = (3/16π)(F_Π/Λ)^4 m_Π (only channel for Π^±); Π^0_{u,d} also γγ, γZ, ZZ, WW.
  - Production: pp→Π resonant; ud̄→Π^+, dū→Π^-, uū→Π^0_u, dd̄→Π^0_d.

  - Phenomenology table (1775–1799): topologies for f=e,μ,τ,ν with composite partners E, M, T, N and final states ℓ±(ℓ∓qq′), ℓ±ℓ∓J, ν(νqq′).

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )
433:     return ordered

439: def _block_entries(p: Parameter, sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> set:
440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""
441:     if not p.is_tensor:
442:         return {(p.order_block,)} if p.order_block is not None else set()
443:     entries = set()
444:     for r in p.value_rules:
445:         m = re.fullmatch(rf"\s*{re.escape(p.name)}\s*\[([0-9,\s]+)\]\s*", r.lhs)
446:         if m:
447:             entries.add(tuple(int(x) for x in m.group(1).split(",")))
448:     if entries:
449:         return entries
450:     ranges = [range(1, sizes.get(i, 3) + 1) for i in p.indices]
451:     out = {()}
452:     for rg in ranges:
453:         out = {e + (k,) for e in out for k in rg}
454:     return out

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
458:     """External parameters that share an LHA block must not share an entry.
459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO
462:     with one name defined twice, and MadGraph rejects the model ("name VLq1x1
463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():
471:         owner: Dict[tuple, str] = {}
472:         for p in ps:
473:             for e in sorted(_block_entries(p, sizes)):

476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )

263: \section{Four-fermion operators and contact interactions}\label{contact}
264: 
265: The SM parity-violating (chiral) gauge symmetries and spontaneous/explicit breaking of these symmetries for the $W$ and $Z$ gauge boson 
266: masses and the hierarchy pattern of fermion masses have been at the 
267: centre of conceptual elaboration for possible scenarios beyond. The No-Go theorem \cite{Nielsen:1981xu, 1981PhLB..105..219N} shows that as a renormalizable quantum field theory at infrared (IR) low energies, the SM {\it bilinear} fermion Lagrangian at ultraviolet (UV) cutoff $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ suffers theoretical inconsistencies with SM chiral gauge symmetries and fermion spectra at low energies. 
268: It implies that the BSM Lagrangian at $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ should have {\it quadrilinear} operators \cite{Xue:2016dpl, Xue2017}
269: \begin{eqnarray}
270: \sum_{f=1,2,3}G_{\rm cut}\, \Big[\bar\psi^{f}_{_L}\psi^{f}_{_R}\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L}\Big]_{q=0,-1,2/3,-1/3},\quad G_{\rm cut}\propto \Lambda^{-2}_{\rm cut},
271: \label{q1}
272: \end{eqnarray}
273: which is SM gauge symmetric four-fermion interactions of left- and right-handed fermions ($\psi^f_L,\psi^f_R$) in the SM charge sector ``$q$'' and flavour family ``$f$''. They are four-fermion operators of Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) or Einstein-Cartan type. Their origins at the scale $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ are due to unknown grand unified interaction or quantum gravity dynamics.  
274: 
275: The strong four-fermion coupling $g_{\rm cut }\propto G_{\rm cut}\Lambda^2_{\rm cut}$ dynamics leads to composite bosons $\Pi^{f}\sim (\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L})$ and fermions $F^{f}_R\sim \psi^{f}_{_R} (\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L})\sim \psi^{f}_{_R}\Pi^{f}$ \cite{Xue1996, Xue2000, Xue2000a}. They 
276: are represented by the
277: mass (pole) and form factor (residue) of propagators, behaving as elementary particles after form-factor renormalisation. These composite particles carry SM quantum numbers and couple to massless SM gauge bosons. Their massive spectra preserve SM gauge symmetries, and constituents can 
278: be leptons, quarks or leptoquarks. There exists a UV fixed point $g^*_{\rm cut}$ and scaling domain, which realises an SM gauge symmetric, renormalizable {\it bilinear and dimensional-4} Lagrangian of composite bosons and fermions at the composite scale $\Lambda\ll \Lambda_{\rm cut}$ \cite{Xue2014, Xue2017}. 
279: As the energy scale decreases below $\Lambda$, the effective theory undergoes \cite{Xue2023} a phase transition of composite particles decay into constituents and spontaneous SM symmetries breaking via the top-quark channel $(\bar t_Lt_R\bar t_R t_L)$, realising the $\bar tt$-composite Higgs boson  
280: at the electroweak scale $v\approx 246$ GeV \cite{Bardeen1990}. The scale $\Lambda\approx 5.1$ TeV is estimated by using the top quark and Higgs boson masses and extrapolating the renormalization-group solution to the high-energy regime \cite{Xue2013}.
281: 
282: In this section we describe the four-fermion operators and contact interactions that are relevant for the study of the phenomenology of the composite bosons at $pp$ or $ep$  collisions, 
283: including the LHC, which will be detailed in Sec.~\ref{PhenomenologyCompositeFermions}.
284: 
285: We consider, among four-fermion operators (\ref{q1}) in introduction, the following SM gauge-symmetric and fermion-number conserving four-fermion operators, 
286: \begin{eqnarray}
287: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_Le_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})
288: +(\bar\ell^{i}_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
289: \label{bhlql}
290: \end{eqnarray}
291: and
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}\ell_{Li})
294: +(\bar\ell^{i}_Le_{R})(\bar e_{R}\ell_{Li})\right]+ {\rm h.c.}\nonumber\\
295: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\ell_{Li})
296: +(\bar\ell^{i}_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\ell_{Li})\right]+ {\rm h.c.}
297: \label{bhlql1}
298: \end{eqnarray}
299: and
300: \begin{eqnarray}
301: &&G\left[(\bar\psi_{Lia}\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}\psi_{Lia})
302: +(\bar\psi_{Lia}e_{R})(\bar e_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
303: \label{bhlql2}\\
304: &&G\left[(\bar\psi^{bi}_Lu_{Rb})(\bar u^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})+(\bar\psi^{bi}_Ld_{Rb})(\bar d^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
305: \label{qbhlql}
306: \end{eqnarray}
307: being the SM doublet $\ell^i_L=(\nu^e_L,e_L)$ and singlet $e_{R}$ with an additional right-handed neutrino $\nu^e_{R}$ for leptons;
308: $\psi_{Lia}=(u_{La},d_{La})$ and $u^a_{R}, d^a_{R}$ for quarks, 
309: where the color $a,b$ and $SU_L(2)$-isospin $i$ indexes are summed over.
310: Eqs. (\ref{bhlql})-(\ref{qbhlql}) 
311: are for the first family only, as a representative of the three fermion families.
312: The SM left- and right-handed fermions are mass eigenstates, their masses are negligible 
313: in TeV-energy regime and small mixing among three families encoded 
314: in $G$ is also neglected \cite{xue2016_2}.
315: 
316: From Eqs. (\ref{bhlql}), (\ref{bhlql1}) and (\ref{bhlql2}), we give explicitly quark-lepton interactions of three types,
317: \begin{eqnarray}
318: &&G\left[(\bar e_Le_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}d_{La})
319: +(\bar\nu^{e}_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}u_{La})+ (\bar\nu^{e}_Le_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
320: \label{bhlqlex}\\
321: &&G\left[(\bar\nu^e_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\nu^e_{L})+
322: (\bar e_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}e_{L})
323: +(\bar\nu^e_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\nu^e_{L})+
324: (\bar e_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}e_{L})\right] + {\rm h.c.},\nonumber\\
325: &&G\left[(\bar u^a_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}u^a_{L})
326: +(\bar d^a_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}d^a_{L})+ (\bar u^a_L e_{R})(\bar e_{R}u^a_{L})
327: +(\bar d^a_L e_{R})(\bar e_{R}d^a_{L})\right] + {\rm h.c.},\nonumber
328: \end{eqnarray}
329: for the first generation. $\nu^e,e,u,d \rightarrow \nu^\mu,\mu,c,s$ for the second generation, and $\nu^e,e,u,d \rightarrow \nu^\tau,\tau,t,b$ for the third generation.

482: \subsection{Contact interaction of composite bosons, quarks and leptons}\label{spqq}
483: 
484: As shown in Fig.~\ref{compositeBv}, 
485: the effective coupling between composite boson 
486: and its two constituents can be written as an effective contact interaction, 
487: \begin{eqnarray}
488: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^\pm}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})\Pi^- + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlB}\\
489: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_d}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar d^a_{R} d_{La})\Pi^0_d + {\rm h.c.},
490: \label{iqlBd}\\
491: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_u}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar u^a_{R} u_{La})\Pi^0_u + {\rm h.c.},
492: \label{iqlBu}
493: \end{eqnarray}
494: and 
495: \begin{eqnarray}
496: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R}u_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql}\\
497: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{-1/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar\nu^e_{R}d_{La})\Pi^{-1/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql1}\\
498: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \nu^e_{R}u_{La}) \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a} + {\rm h.c.},
499: \label{iqlBuql}\\
500: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R} d_{La})\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a} + {\rm h.c.},
501: \label{iqlBdql}
502: \end{eqnarray}
503: where $g_{_{\rm Y}}=(F_\Pi/\Lambda)^2$.
504: Appropriate normalizing the composite boson $\Pi$ with the 
505: form factor $(g^*/F_\Pi)^2$ in Eqs. (\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}),  
506: the effective contact interaction in Eqs. (\ref{ciqlB}-\ref{iqlBu}) and (\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}) can be expressed as a dimensionless Yukawa coupling $g_{_{\rm Y}}$, 
507: whose value, corresponding to $F_\Pi$ value, 
508: can be different for composite bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}) and (\ref{nB5/3}-\ref{uB2/3}), but we do not consider such difference here.
509: These are relevant contact interactions for phenomenological studies of possible inelastic channels of composite-fermion production and decay in  $pp$ or $ep$ collisions.
510:

\subsection{Contact interaction of composite bosons, quarks and leptons}\label{spqq}

As shown in Fig.~\ref{compositeBv}, 
the effective coupling between composite boson 
and its two constituents can be written as an effective contact interaction, 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^\pm}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})\Pi^- + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlB}\\
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_d}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar d^a_{R} d_{La})\Pi^0_d + {\rm h.c.},
\label{iqlBd}\\
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_u}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar u^a_{R} u_{La})\Pi^0_u + {\rm h.c.},
\label{iqlBu}
\end{eqnarray}
and 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R}u_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql}\\
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{-1/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar\nu^e_{R}d_{La})\Pi^{-1/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql1}\\
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \nu^e_{R}u_{La}) \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a} + {\rm h.c.},
\label{iqlBuql}\\
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R} d_{La})\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a} + {\rm h.c.},
\label{iqlBdql}
\end{eqnarray}
where $g_{_{\rm Y}}=(F_\Pi/\Lambda)^2$.
Appropriate normalizing the composite boson $\Pi$ with the 
form factor $(g^*/F_\Pi)^2$ in Eqs. (\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}),  
the effective contact interaction in Eqs. (\ref{ciqlB}-\ref{iqlBu}) and (\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}) can be expressed as a dimensionless Yukawa coupling $g_{_{\rm Y}}$, 
whose value, corresponding to $F_\Pi$ value, 
can be different for composite bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}) and (\ref{nB5/3}-\ref{uB2/3}), but we do not consider such difference here.
These are relevant contact interactions for phenomenological studies of possible inelastic channels of composite-fermion production and decay in  $pp$ or $ep$ collisions.

\red{We discuss the issue of generation mixing for four different charged types of LQ states: $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$, $\Pi^{-1/3}_{a}$  $\Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}$ and $\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}$ in Table \ref{qnuP0ql}. Each type has three copies due to generations, taking as example $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar e_{R}u_{La})$, $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar \mu_{R}c_{La})$ and $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})$. If the LQ $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$ is produced by, then decay to its constituents in the same generation, the Yukawa coupling $g_Y\sim {\mathcal O}(1)$ as given in Eqs.(\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}). Now we consider $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$ is produced by $e$ and $u$ of the first family, and the branching ratio of decaying to $\tau$ and $t$ of the third family. The Yukawa coupling $g_Y\sim {\mathcal O}(1)$ for $e$ and $u$ production, and another Yukawa coupling $g'_Y$ for decaying to $\tau$ and $t$. The Yukawa coupling $g'_Y$ is a new parameter and $g'_Y < g_Y$, possibly $g'_Y\ll g_Y$ for the following reasons. The left- and right-handed fields of leptons and quarks, which make composite bosons and fermions, are the SM gauge eigenstates in each generation. They are the same as the mass eigenstates without considering generation mixing. If we need to consider the mixing, see the unitary flavour transformations eqs (15,16) for quarks and eqs (23, 24) for leptons in my article JHEP 2016 ref. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.01266.pdf. Using these unitary transformations $U^{\nu,\ell, u,d}_{L,R}$, we can rewrite the Yukawa couplings (\ref{ciqlB})-(\ref{iqlBdql}) by associating two unitary matrices $(U)^\dagger U$ which are unknown. As example,  by interacting (\ref{ciqlBql}) the $e$ and $u$ produced $\Pi_a^{5/3}$ will decay to $\tau$ and $t$ by interacting
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(U^\dagger_R U_L) (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.} = g'_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.} ,\label{ciqlBqlmix}
\end{eqnarray}
where $g'_{_{\rm Y}} = g_{_{\rm Y}}(U^\dagger_R U_L)$, 
and the notation $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ stands for relevant unitary transformations between generations considered. The general mixing matrix $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ of leptoquark sector, see eq (35) of my JHEP 2016, has its analogies CKM matrix in quark sector, PMNS matrix in lepton sector. In conclusion, the general mixing matrix $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ is totally unknown, the effective way for dealing with composite states of different generations but the same SM quantum numbers is to introduce a new Yukawa coupling. These discussions also apply to the three nonLQ composite bosons $\Pi^-$, $\Pi^0_u$ and $\Pi^0_d$ see eqs. (\ref{ciqlB})-(\ref{iqlBd}). It can be considered as a general rule for considering the initial and final states are not in the same family.}

There are three types operators (\ref{bhlql}), (\ref{bhlql1}) and (\ref{bhlql2}) that can form LQ composite fermion states.

922: is an axial anomaly vertex, as a result of a triangle quark loop and standard renormalization procedure in SM. The color factor $N_c=3$ comes from the trace over color space of quarks in loop. The contact interaction (\ref{PiGG}) can be written as 
923: \begin{eqnarray}
924: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^0}_{\tilde G\tilde G'} = \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ gg^\prime N_c}{4\pi^2
925: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\frac{1}{4}(F^{\rho\mu})(F^{\prime\sigma\nu})\Pi^0_i.
926: \label{PiGG1} 
927: \end{eqnarray}
928: \red{These amplitudes or effective interacting Lagrangians are the same, independent of quark types and masses in triangle loop. Therefore, it is the same and generalized for all generations. In addition, $\Pi^0_{u,d}$ decay to two gluons
929: \begin{eqnarray}
930: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& \tilde g
931: + \tilde g,\label{cpgg}
932: \end{eqnarray}
933: via the contact interaction
934: \begin{eqnarray}
935: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^0}_{\tilde g\tilde g'} &=& \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ g_s^2/2}{4\pi^2

937: &=& \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ g_s^2/2}{4\pi^2
938: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\frac{1}{4}(G^{\rho\mu}_a)(G^{\prime\sigma\nu}_a)\Pi^0_i,
939: \label{PiGGg} 
940: \end{eqnarray}
941: where the strong coupling $g_s$ and $\alpha_s=g_s^2/(4\pi)$, the trace over color space gives $\tr(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2$, leading to $(G^{\rho\mu}_a)(G^{\prime\sigma\nu}_a)$ summed over color index $a$, see Ref.~\cite{anomalyS}.
942: Here we note that the normal $\pi^0$ meson  $\pi^0=\bar u\gamma_5 u-\bar d\gamma_5 d$ in the $SU(3)$ quark model, the $u$ and $d$ color charges are the same. Thus their triangle diagram contributions to the anomaly, i.e., $\pi^0$ decays to two gluons, are the same, but opposite in sign, therefore exactly canceled each other. As a result, the total amplitude of the normal $\pi^0$ decay to two gluons is zero. This is not the case for its decay to two photons, since the $u$ and $d$ have different electric charges. In our case, $\Pi^0_u$ and $\Pi^0_d$ are different states, and both decay to two gluons and amplitudes are the same.}

The neutral channels are
945: \begin{eqnarray}
946: \Pi^\pm &\rightarrow& \gamma + W^\pm,\label{cpgz+} \\
947: \Pi^\pm &\rightarrow& Z^0 +W^\pm,\label{cpww+}
948: 
949: 
950: \end{eqnarray}

952: \begin{eqnarray}
953: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^\pm}_{\tilde G\tilde G'} = \frac{ gg^\prime N_c}{4\pi^2
954: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}(\partial^\rho A^\mu)(\partial^\sigma A^{\prime\nu})\Pi^\pm.
955: \label{PiGG1+} 
956: \end{eqnarray}
957: The reason is that $\Pi^\pm$ masses are larger than the SM gauge bosons $W^\pm$ and $Z^0$.
958: There are two possibilities in Eq. (\ref{PiGG1+}). (i) $\Pi^+AW^+$ interaction comes from the triangle loop made by quarks $uud$:
959: \begin{eqnarray}

962: \label{PiGG1+1} 
963: \end{eqnarray}

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
458:     """External parameters that share an LHA block must not share an entry.
459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO
462:     with one name defined twice, and MadGraph rejects the model ("name VLq1x1
463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():
471:         owner: Dict[tuple, str] = {}
472:         for p in ps:
473:             for e in sorted(_block_entries(p, sizes)):
474:                 if e in owner and owner[e] != p.name:
475:                     raise ValueError(
476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )

class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_preamble):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_preamble[{i}]")
        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_blocks):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_blocks[{i}]")

        names = [p.name for p in self.parameters]
        dupes = sorted({x for x in names if names.count(x) > 1})
        if dupes:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate parameter names: {dupes}")
        sizes = dict(_INDEX_SIZE, **{d.name: d.size for d in self.index_decls})
        _check_block_collisions(self.parameters, sizes)

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

1297: We turn to the pair production of composite particles (fermion and boson) by SM gauge bosons, in particularly by gluons. The composite particles are made of SM quarks and leptons. Therefore, they have SM quantum numbers to couple to SM gauge bosons. These couplings in principle are new parameters of the theory. However, If SM gauge bosons, here we particularly mean gluons,  have energies comparable to composite scale, namely the composite particle masses $M_{F,\Pi}\sim {\mathcal O}(TeV)$, then gluons interact with the quark constitute inside the composite particle. In this case, the strength of gluon coupling to composite particle can be approximately represented by QCD strong coupling $g_s=\sqrt{\alpha_s}$. This is the case for the pair productions of composite particle $\Pi, F$ and anti composite particle $\Pi^\dagger, F^\dagger$ by gluon and gluon collisions,
1298: \begin{eqnarray}
1299: g+g~&\rightarrow& ~ \Pi + \Pi^\dagger ~~{\rm or}~~F + F^\dagger,\label{FqqBql} 
1300: \end{eqnarray}
1301: The reason is that in center of mass frame, gluon and gluon collision energy must be larger than the energy threshold 
1302: $2 M_{F,\Pi}$ to produce two composte particles flying apart, back-to-back. The composite particle and anti composite particle have the same mass. Here, we may consider the lepton-quark composite states, since their decay modes (topologies) are distinct from the SM QCD background.  But the discussions are the same for the pair productions of other composite particles in general.
1303: 
1304: This situation is very much like the Breit-Wheeler process of electron-positron pair production by light-light collision $\gamma+\gamma \rightarrow e^++e^-$. Thus, learning from the QED calculation as shown two tree-level Feynman diagrams in Fig.~\ref{ggpair}, we can write the cross-section as 
1305: \begin{eqnarray}
1306: \sigma_{gg\rightarrow FF^\dagger ~{\rm or}~ \Pi\Pi^\dagger}~&\approx& ~ \frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{\alpha_s}{M_{F,\Pi}}\right)^2(1-\hat\beta^2)
1307: \Big[2\hat\beta^2(\hat\beta^2-2)+(3-\hat\beta^4)\ln\Big(\frac{1+\hat\beta^2}{1-\hat\beta^2}\Big)\Big],\quad \hat\beta^2=\frac{|{\bf p}|}{{\mathcal E}_{gg}}\label{ggpaircross} 
1308: \end{eqnarray}
1309: where ${\mathcal E}_{gg}$ is the two gluons colision energy in CM. Here we use approximation $\sigma_{gg\rightarrow FF^\dagger ~{\rm or}~ \Pi\Pi^\dagger}~\approx ...$, because we approximate the coupling between gluon and composite particle to be the QCD coupling $g_s$. For the energy ${\mathcal E}_{gg}\gg M_{F,\Pi}$, the pair-production cross-section yields
1310: \begin{eqnarray}
1311: \sigma_{gg\rightarrow FF^\dagger ~{\rm or}~ \Pi\Pi^\dagger}~&\approx& ~ \pi \left(\frac{\alpha_s}{M_{F,\Pi}}\right)^2\left(\frac{M_{F,\Pi}}{{\mathcal E}_{gg}}\right)^2.
1312: \label{ggpaircrossa} 
1313: \end{eqnarray}
1314: Only the composite particle masses are involved, no other new parameters like $g_{_Y}$. This process should have the biggest cross section (absorption of gluons), if the gluons collision energy is over the energy threshold $M_{F,\Pi}$ of pair production of composite particles. The decay modes of back-to-back composite particles follow discussions before.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing

def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
    out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(text):
        if text.startswith("(*", i):
            depth += 1
            i += 2
            continue
        if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
            depth -= 1
            i += 2
            continue
        if depth == 0:
            out.append(text[i])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set

HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"

# Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
# not be named after (rule 10).
FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
              "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
              "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
             "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
             "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}

# Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
_SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
    SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
_i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
              "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
             "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}

FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
               "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
               "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
               "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
               "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
               "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
               "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
               "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
               "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
               "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}


@dataclass
class Finding:
    rule: str
    stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn

In Eqs.~(\ref{bhlql2}), each four-fermion operator has the two possibilities to form composite fermions, listed in Tables \ref{QF0+} and \ref{qQF0+}.
Up to a form factor, $E$ ($N$) indicate a composite fermion composed by an electron (a neutrino) and a color lepton quark pair $\Pi_a$, and its superscript for electric charge. In Eq.~(\ref{bhlql2}), there are four independent composite fields $F$: $N_{Ra}^{2/3}$, $N_{Ra}^{-1/3}$, $E^{2/3}_{Ra}$, $E^{-1/3}_{Ra}$
and
their Hermitian conjugates:
$\bar N^{-2/3}_{La}=(N_{Ra}^{2/3})^\dagger\gamma_0$,  
$\bar N^{1/3}_{La}=(N_{Ra}^{-1/3})^\dagger\gamma_0$, $\bar E^{-2/3}_{La}=(E^{2/3}_{Ra})^\dagger\gamma_0$, $\bar E^{1/3}_{La}=(E^{-1/3}_{Ra})^\dagger\gamma_0$. See tables \ref{QF0+} and \ref{qQF0+}. 




They carry SM quantum numbers $t^i_{3L},Y$, and 
$Q_i=Y+t^i_{3L}$, which are the sum of SM quantum numbers ($t^i_{3L}, Y, Q_i$) of their constituents, i.e., the elementary leptons and quarks in the same SM family \cite{xue2017}, listed in Table \ref{qnuF0+} and \ref{qQF0+}, so that the contact interactions in Eq. (\ref{c1}) are SM gauge symmetric. 

The four composite fields $F$: 
$N_{Ra}^{2/3}$, $N_{Ra}^{-1/3}$, $E^{2/3}_{Ra}$, $E^{-1/3}_{Ra}$ are two-component right-handed Wely fermions. 

They form two right-handed SU(2) doublets: (i) $N_{Ra}=(N^{2/3}_{Ra},N^{-1/3}_{Ra}) = \Pi^a_{1/6}\nu^e_R$ of u channel hypercharge 1/6 +0= 1/6, (ii) $E_{Ra}=(E^{2/3}_{Ra},E^{-1/3}_{Ra}) = \Pi_{7/6}e_R$ of d channel hypercharge 7/6 -1= 1/6, where the 
SU(2) LQ composite boson doublets: $\Pi^a_{1/6}=(\Pi^{2/3}_{u_a},\Pi^{-1/3}_a)$  of u channel the hypercharge 1/6, and $\Pi^a_{7/6}=(\Pi^{5/3}_a,\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a})$  of d channel the hypercharge 7/6.

The SU(2) doublet massive Dirac fermions (four spinor components) are: (i)  $N^a_D=(N^{2/3}_{Ra}+u_{La},N^{-1/3}_{Ra}+d_{La})$ of hypercharge 1/6 and Dirac mass term $M_F\bar N_D N_D$; (ii)  $E^a_D=(E^{2/3}_{Ra}+u_{La},E^{-1/3}_{Ra}+d_{La})$ of hypercharge 1/6 and Dirac mass term $M_F\bar E_D E_D$.

There are two left-handed SU(2) singlets: (i) $N^s_{La} = (\nu^e_L,e_L)\Pi^{a}_{1/6}$ of u channel of hypercharge 1/6-1/2=-1/3= charge, (ii) $E^s_{La}=(\nu^e_L,e_L)\Pi^a_{7/6}$ of d channel of hypercharge 7/6-1/2=2/3= charge, where the 
SU(2) LQ composite boson doublets: $\Pi^{a}_{1/6}=(\Pi^{2/3}_{u_a},\Pi^{-1/3}_a)$  of u channel the hypercharge 1/6, and $\Pi^{a}_{7/6}=(\Pi^{5/3}_a,\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a})$  of d channel the hypercharge 7/6.

The SU(2) singlet massive Dirac fermions (four spinor components) are: (i)  $N^s_{Da}=(N^s_{La}+d_{Ra})$ of hypercharge -1/3, charge e=Y=-1/3 and Dirac mass term 
$M_F\bar N_{Da} N_{Da}$; (ii)  $E^s_{Da}=(E^s_{La}+u_{Ra})$ of hypercharge 2/3,  charge e=Y=2/3 and Dirac mass term 
$M_F\bar E_{Da} E_{Da}$.

display.text:
interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_preamble):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_preamble[{i}]")
        for i, raw in enumerate(self.raw_blocks):
            _require_balanced(raw, f"raw_blocks[{i}]")

        names = [p.name for p in self.parameters]
        dupes = sorted({x for x in names if names.count(x) > 1})
        if dupes:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate parameter names: {dupes}")
        sizes = dict(_INDEX_SIZE, **{d.name: d.size for d in self.index_decls})
        _check_block_collisions(self.parameters, sizes)

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self
